agent_exit_status_fix.found_by: the rehearsal agent's own log after a planned SIGTERM stop

before.traceback: rclpy._rclpy_pybind11.RCLError: failed to shutdown: rcl_shutdown already called on the given context - raised from the shutdown() call inside main()'s finally, after rclpy's signal handler had already closed the context
before.consequence: every planned 停止/回退 left a stack trace as the last thing in the car log, and any statement added after that call would have been unreachable; the safety work before it (stop_session, chassis zero, HTTP shutdown) did run, which is why both sessions still finalised raw_ready

after.log_tail: [INFO] [lelab_mobile_agent]: agent stopping: ExternalShutdownException followed by rclpy's own 'Failed to publish log message to rosout: publisher's context is invalid' line, which stays because the context is already gone
changes: main() now catches PLANNED_STOP_ERRORS = (KeyboardInterrupt, ExternalShutdownException) and logs the reason instead of escaping
teardown moved into _teardown(agent, server) and calls rclpy.shutdown() only when rclpy.ok() is still true
PLANNED_STOP_ERRORS falls back to (KeyboardInterrupt,) if a build has no ExternalShutdownException, so the deployed agent still imports

verified_live: SIGTERM to the exec'd agent pid (recorded in car/agent.pid, cross-checked against ss -ltnp) -> exit 1 with RCLError traceback before the change
same stop after the change -> exit 0, no traceback, port released, no leftover rehearsal process (only the verified pid was signalled; no blanket kill)
agent_exit_status_fix.mutation_check: restoring the unconditional rclpy.shutdown() makes _teardown raise 'rcl_shutdown already called on the given context', i.e. the second test goes red

second_exception_class_found.observation: the restarted agent's planned SIGTERM stop did not surface as ExternalShutdownException at all: rclpy raised RCLError 'failed to initialize wait set: the given context is not valid' from _wait_for_ready_callbacks, which the class tuple did not cover, so that run again printed a traceback
second_exception_class_found.fix: main() now catches BaseException and asks _is_planned_stop(): the class tuple OR `not rclpy.ok()`; anything else re-raises with its traceback intact
second_exception_class_found.why_the_context_is_the_witness: nothing in this process tears the context down before main() returns from the spin loop, so a dead context means somebody asked the process to stop regardless of where the signal landed
second_exception_class_found.pinned_by: tools/ros2_collection/tests/test_agent_exit_teardown.py::TeardownTests::test_the_context_decides_which_rclpy_error_counts_as_a_planned_stop (a RuntimeError with a live context must still count as a fault)
